title: Which two digits can you swap to pass a target?
description: Kavya's lucky-draw ticket wins a prize if it is above a target after one swap. The video finds a swap that makes the thousands digit big enough.
teaching_notes: One idea: to pass a target, the leftmost place must be big enough, so bring a big digit to the front. Watch for a swap that leaves the thousands digit small.

source: Let Us Do 5 (a), digit swap in 1,478
video_script.why: The child knows a swap changes the number but has not yet chosen a swap to beat a target.
video_script.substitution: The thousands digit must be five or more, so swap a digit that is five or more into the thousands place.
video_script.anchor: Kavya's lucky-draw ticket with a prize target
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu swaps four and seven again and thinks the ticket is bigger. The thousands digit is still one, so the ticket stays below five thousand, five hundred.
video_script.payoff_line: the ticket becomes seven thousand, four hundred and eighteen

final_answer.spoken: seven thousand four hundred and eighteen by swapping one and seven

maths_rules: ticket 1,478 has digits 1, 4, 7, 8; swapping 7 and 4 gives 1,748
to be larger than 5,500 the thousands digit must be 5 or more; only 7 and 8 are 5 or more
slip: swap 4 and 7 gives 1,748; the thousands digit is still 1; 1,748 < 5,500
video_script.design: Exercise: swap two digits to pass a target. Hint: the thousands digit must be five or more. The ticket with four digit boxes stays on the stage.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a lucky-draw ticket marked 1,478 with digit boxes; a prize board marked above 5,500; an empty box

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.swap: the 7 and 4 swap and the ticket shows 1,748, then it swaps back
marks.ask: a prize board marked above 5,500 and an empty box appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='ticket'/>Kavya's lucky-draw ticket shows one thousand, four hundred and seventy-eight.
<bookmark mark='swap'/>If she swaps the seven and the four, it reads one thousand, seven hundred and forty-eight.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>A prize goes to any ticket above five thousand, five hundred. Which two digits can she swap to win?

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still and gets an accent underline

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: the ticket digits 1, 4, 7, 8 in boxes; the thousands box is marked five or more; a question mark over the digits

marks.need: the thousands box is marked five or more
marks.dig: the four digit boxes 1, 4, 7 and 8 glow
marks.try: a question mark appears over the digits

narration: <bookmark mark='need'/>To be larger than five thousand, five hundred, the thousands digit must be five or more.
<bookmark mark='dig'/>Look at the digits one, four, seven and eight.
<bookmark mark='try'/>Which of them is five or more? Try again with this.

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows swap 4 and 7; the ticket shows 1,748 with the thousands digit 1 circled; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.chintu: Chintu's bubble appears with swap 4 and 7
marks.still: the ticket shows 1,748 with the thousands digit 1 circled
marks.strike: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Swap four and seven again, because it gives a bigger ticket.
<bookmark mark='still'/>That ticket reads one thousand, seven hundred and forty-eight.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>The thousands digit is still one, so it is far below five thousand, five hundred.

beats.on_screen: the 7 and the 8 glow; the 1 and the 7 swap places; the ticket reads 7,418; the answer card shows 7,418

marks.only: the 7 and the 8 glow, the 1 and the 4 fade
marks.pay: the ticket reads 7,418 and the answer card appears

narration: <bookmark mark='only'/>Only seven and eight are five or more.
<bookmark mark='front'/>Move the seven to the front, and swap the one and the seven.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>The ticket becomes seven thousand, four hundred and eighteen.

beats.on_screen: 7,418 > 5,500 is written; a second ticket shows 8,471 as another answer

marks.alt: the ticket shows 8,471 as a second answer

narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Seven thousand is more than five thousand, five hundred, so the ticket wins.
<bookmark mark='alt'/>Swapping the one and the eight gives eight thousand, four hundred and seventy-one, which also works.

beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the ticket; two lines appear: look at the thousands digit; five or more is above 5,500; the thousands digit of the new ticket is circled

marks.cmp: the line look at the thousands digit appears
marks.rule: the line five or more is above 5,500 appears
marks.ask: the thousands digit of the new ticket is circled

narration: <bookmark mark='cmp'/>To check, look at the thousands digit of the new number.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>If it is five or more, the number is above five thousand, five hundred.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Is the thousands digit of your new ticket five or more?
